LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASS: PREPOSITIONS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we tell others exactly where people and things are?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences
2. use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASS: PREPOSITIONS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASS: PREPOSITIONS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions to a partner. (skill: use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences.
3. Practise this skill: use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we tell others exactly where people and things are?
2. How do we show the position of people and things?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify prepositions of position and direction in sentences.
5. Be able to: use prepositions correctly in oral and written contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
